step: Apply for Employment Visa at Indian Mission Abroad
authority: Indian Mission Abroad / Ministry of External Affairs

step: Verify minimum annual salary threshold of USD 25,000
field_label: Minimum Gross Salary: USD 25,000 per annum
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employment Visa requires the foreign national to be in receipt of a salary of not less than USD 25,000 per annum. Exceptions exist for ethnic Indian professionals and language teachers.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Indian CTC packages are typically expressed in INR. The employment contract submitted with the visa application must demonstrate the USD 25,000 threshold either in USD or with an explicit currency conversion note; a rupee-only contract can trigger embassy rejection without explanation.
non_obvious_action_required: Confirm the offer letter or employment contract states gross annual compensation equivalent to at least USD 25,000. Add a USD salary clause or certified conversion statement before submitting the visa application.
source: MHA – Consolidated Guidelines on Visa, Immigration and Foreigners Registration

step: Obtain employer sponsorship documents for visa application
field_label: Employer Support Letter; Employment Contract; Company Registration Certificate

step: Confirm Employment Visa is employer-specific and role-specific
field_label: Visa Restriction: Tied to Named Employer and Role
deadline_label: Before accepting offer or agreeing intra-group transfer
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employment Visa is granted to work for a specific employer in a specific role. A change of employer requires a fresh Employment Visa application.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Intra-group transfers — for example from a parent company to an Indian subsidiary or between two Indian group entities — still require a new Employment Visa if the legal employer entity changes. HR teams managing internal mobility routinely miss this, assuming the existing visa covers the new entity.
non_obvious_action_required: Before any employer-of-record change, secondment, or intra-group transfer, seek immigration counsel and plan for a 4–8 week visa reapplication lead time.
source: MHA – Consolidated Guidelines on Visa, Immigration and Foreigners Registration

step: Apply for PAN card (Form 49AA) for foreign nationals
authority: Income Tax Department of India / Protean (NSDL)
deadline_label: As soon as possible after arrival; required before employer can issue Form 16

step: Police reporting for nationals of notified countries
deadline_label: Within 24 hours of arrival for nationals of notified countries (see visa stamp)
non_obvious_official_guidance: Nationals of certain countries are required to report to the local police station within 24 hours of arrival as a condition stamped on the visa, pursuant to MHA orders.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The list of notified nationalities includes Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Iraq, Iran, Sudan, and others. HR teams managing employees from these countries consistently miss this requirement — it is stated only on the visa stamp itself, not in any onboarding checklist. Non-compliance creates an adverse immigration record.
non_obvious_action_required: On Day 1, check the employee's visa stamp for a 'Report to Police' condition. If present, accompany the employee to the nearest police station before Day 2. The requirement applies only to nationals of notified countries — not all foreign employees.

step: Notify employer of Indian residential address for TDS configuration
field_label: Employee Address and PAN for Payroll TDS Setup
source: Income Tax India – TDS on Salary (Section 192)

step: Collect physical PAN card and furnish to employer for Form 16
authority: Income Tax Department of India / Protean (NSDL)
deadline_label: Within 15–20 working days of application; required before Form 16 issuance

step: Assess income tax residency status: 182-day rule and RNOR eligibility
field_label: Residential Status: Resident / RNOR / Non-Resident (Section 6, IT Act 1961)
deadline_label: Before close of first Indian financial year (31 March)
non_obvious_official_guidance: A person is Resident in India if present for 182 days or more in the financial year (1 April–31 March). A Resident qualifies as Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident (RNOR) if they were Non-Resident in 9 of the preceding 10 years, or were present in India for 729 days or fewer across the preceding 7 years.
non_obvious_actual_reality: RNOR status means only India-sourced income is taxable — foreign income and overseas assets are excluded from Indian tax for up to 2–3 financial years after arrival. Most arriving foreign employees and their HR teams are unaware of RNOR and file ITRs as full Residents, materially overpaying tax. RNOR eligibility must be established in the first year or the benefit cannot be claimed retroactively.
non_obvious_action_required: Immediately on arrival, document prior-year India residence history. If RNOR conditions are met, engage a tax professional to file the ITR reflecting RNOR status and exclude foreign-sourced income from Indian taxable income before the first year-end.

step: Employer configures Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) on salary under Section 192
form_name: Form 16 (annual TDS certificate issued to employee)
field_label: TDS on Salary: Section 192, Income Tax Act 1961
deadline_label: From first payroll run in India
source: Income Tax India – TDS on Salary (Section 192)

step: Register foreign employee as International Worker under EPF scheme
field_label: International Worker: EPF Contributions at 12% of Basic Wages
deadline_label: From date of joining; contribution due from first payroll run
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign nationals working in India are classified as International Workers under the EPF and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952. Both employee and employer must contribute 12% of basic wages to EPF from the first month of employment, with no salary ceiling exemption.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Many Indian employers incorrectly treat foreign employees as exempt from EPF, unaware that the International Worker provisions make EPF mandatory regardless of salary level — unlike domestic employees who are exempt above ₹15,000 per month. Non-compliance triggers EPFO penalties and can create a block on the departing employee's immigration clearance.
non_obvious_action_required: Register the employee as an International Worker with EPFO from Day 1. Deduct and remit 12% EPF contributions from both employee and employer from the first payroll. Check SSA Certificate of Coverage eligibility before the first payroll run — an exemption may apply.

step: Obtain Social Security Agreement Certificate of Coverage to claim EPF exemption
field_label: SSA Exemption: Certificate of Coverage from Home-Country Authority
deadline_label: Before first EPF contribution; retroactive correction is administratively complex
non_obvious_official_guidance: Under a bilateral Social Security Agreement (SSA), a foreign national who is a citizen of an SSA country and is covered by their home country's social security system may be exempt from EPF contributions in India upon obtaining a Certificate of Coverage issued by the home-country social security authority.
non_obvious_actual_reality: India has SSAs with Germany, South Korea, Japan, France, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Hungary, Denmark, Finland, Sweden, Czech Republic, Norway, Austria, Belgium, Netherlands, Portugal, Australia, Canada, Brazil, and others. HR teams routinely begin EPF deductions without checking SSA status and then face cumbersome refund procedures. The CoC must be obtained from the home-country authority before contributions commence — not after.
non_obvious_action_required: Before the first payroll: (1) check whether the employee's home country has an active SSA with India; (2) if yes, instruct the employee to apply for a Certificate of Coverage from their home-country social security authority; (3) begin EPF deductions only if a valid CoC is not obtained in time.

step: Apply for Aadhaar card after accumulating 182 days of India residence
deadline_label: Eligible after 182 days of residence in India within preceding 12 months
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign nationals who have been resident in India for 182 days or more in the 12 months immediately preceding the date of application are eligible to apply for Aadhaar at a UIDAI-approved enrolment centre.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Aadhaar is increasingly required for KYC purposes — opening bank accounts, obtaining SIM cards, and accessing certain government services. Employees on multi-year postings who delay Aadhaar enrolment find themselves repeatedly unable to complete digital KYC processes. Biometric enrolment appointments and card delivery can take several weeks.
non_obvious_action_required: Track the date the employee accumulates 182 cumulative days of India residence. Initiate Aadhaar enrolment at the nearest UIDAI-approved centre immediately after eligibility is confirmed; do not wait until a specific service requires it.

step: File annual Income Tax Return (ITR-2) by 31 July
form_name: ITR-2 (individuals with foreign income or overseas assets)
field_label: Annual ITR Filing Deadline: 31 July of the Assessment Year
deadline_label: 31 July of the Assessment Year (i.e. within 4 months of financial year end 31 March)

step: Renew FRRO registration before Registration Certificate or visa expiry
field_label: Registration Certificate Renewal (typically annual, aligned to visa validity)
deadline_label: Before expiry of Registration Certificate; apply at least 2 weeks in advance
source: e-FRRO Portal – Foreigners Regional Registration Office

step: Reassess RNOR vs Ordinary Resident status each financial year
field_label: Residential Status Annual Review: RNOR-to-Resident Transition Point
deadline_label: Each April before filing the year's ITR by 31 July
non_obvious_official_guidance: RNOR status is available only while the qualifying conditions under Section 6 of the Income Tax Act are met. Once a foreign employee transitions to Ordinary Resident status, worldwide income — including offshore salary, overseas bank interest, and foreign investments — becomes taxable in India.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Foreign employees assume RNOR benefits continue for the duration of their posting. In practice the transition to Ordinary Resident can occur as early as Year 2 or Year 3 depending on prior India residence history, requiring restructuring of split-payroll arrangements, overseas income reporting, and Schedule FA (Foreign Assets) disclosure in the ITR.
non_obvious_action_required: Each April, recalculate India presence days for the prior financial year and re-check RNOR qualifying conditions. If transitioning to Ordinary Resident status, restructure any offshore salary or split-payroll arrangements before the transition year's ITR filing deadline.

step: Submit EPF withdrawal or transfer claim on departure as International Worker
form_name: Composite Claim Form (Aadhaar-based) or Form 19 / Form 10C
field_label: EPF International Worker Withdrawal on Final Departure from India
deadline_label: On or after final departure from India; submit before balance becomes inoperative (3 years)
non_obvious_official_guidance: An International Worker may withdraw their EPF accumulations upon final departure from India on completion of their Indian posting or at retirement age.
non_obvious_actual_reality: International Workers cannot make partial or early EPF withdrawals (unlike domestic employees). Employers routinely fail to inform departing foreign employees of their accumulated EPF balance — often a significant sum after 2–3 years of mandatory 12% contributions. Unclaimed EPF balances are transferred to EPFO's Inoperative Account after 3 years, complicating recovery.
non_obvious_action_required: Before finalising departure: (1) obtain the EPF account statement via the EPFO member portal; (2) submit the composite withdrawal claim form; (3) confirm with HR that all contributions were correctly deposited. File the claim before the departure date to avoid the inoperative account transfer window.

step: De-register from FRRO and file exit intimation before final departure
field_label: Registration Certificate Surrender on Final Departure
deadline_label: Before or on the final departure date from India
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreigners holding a Registration Certificate must inform the FRRO of their final departure from India. The Registration Certificate is to be surrendered upon exit.
non_obvious_actual_reality: FRRO de-registration is almost universally skipped. Departing employees and HR teams assume the record lapses automatically. An open FRRO registration with no exit entry creates adverse scrutiny on future Indian visa applications — the consular officer sees an unresolved prior registration and may require a manual explanation, delaying or blocking the new visa.
non_obvious_action_required: In the week before final departure, log into the e-FRRO portal and file an exit intimation or de-registration request. Confirm the record is marked closed before boarding the departure flight. Keep a screenshot of the closed status for future visa applications.
source: e-FRRO Portal – Foreigners Regional Registration Office

step: Register with the FRRO/FRO via the e-FRRO portal
deadline_label: within 14 days of arrival for stays over 180 days
non_obvious_official_guidance: Foreign nationals holding a visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the FRRO/FRO within 14 days of first arrival in India via the e-FRRO portal; required documents include passport, visa, arrival stamp, employer letter, and residential address proof.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The e-FRRO portal frequently suffers outages and session timeouts; police verification is conducted at the declared residential address after online submission and can take 2–4 weeks; many banks, landlords, and corporate security teams require a stamped physical Registration Certificate obtainable only by attending the FRRO office in person even after the digital RC is issued online.
non_obvious_action_required: Register on the e-FRRO portal within 14 days of arrival; pre-gather employer sponsorship letter on company letterhead, proof of local address, and passport photos; track police verification status in the portal; download and print the digital RC; confirm with HR and any bank whether a physical FRRO-stamped copy is additionally required and schedule the office visit before the 14-day deadline if so.
source: Bureau of Immigration — e-FRRO Portal (Government of India)
